Primary scientific modeling of human neural/cognitive dynamics. Section 5 explicitly distinguishes its IRF/cognitive questions from engineering performance; Natural Stories fMRI models cortical language-network responses, non-linear BOLD saturation and interactions between structural and string surprisal. This is actual human neural-response research in healthy subjects, not merely NLP evaluated with a brain-data illustration.
Structural supervision improves Transformer syntactic generalization on language test suites; primary subject is linguistic generalization.

Primary experimental question is human sentence-processing mechanism and morphology, tested using reading, eye-tracking and language-network fMRI from 78 subjects. Section 7 fits BOLD responses and interprets differences between latency-based measures and blood oxygenation. The study investigates human neural processing rather than optimizing generic NLP task scores.
CogAlign transfers cognitive signals into general NER, sentiment and relation-extraction representations; objective is generic NLP task performance, not biomedical investigation.

Under the clarified co-primary actual-research/experiments criterion, biomedical extraction is a central substantive validation arm, not an incidental benchmark. Beyond PubMed chemical/disease tagging results, Sections 3.4–3.8 center learning dynamics, lexicon-effort comparison, rule-selection ablations, detailed chemical/disease boundary and semantic errors, and an explainability user study on BC5CDR. Domain-general rule induction and CoNLL validation are real counterevidence to sole biomedical scope but do not negate this co-primary biomedical experimental program. No distinct clinical hypothesis or dataset-majority rule is required.
